items.title: Frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pairs and their real-field encoding
items.reference: scaffold-added necessary formulation prerequisite for the vector PEC scattering theorem (see research/physics-em-sr-40-2026-10-08-batch-40.notes.md)
items.statement: Let $\omega>0$, let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a nonempty open set, and let $c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ be the vacuum constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. (a) [Phasor encoding] For every pair of $C^\infty$ maps $\widetilde E,\widetilde B:D\to\mathbb C^3$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) define the **associated real fields** $$E(x,t):=\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\widetilde E(x)e^{-i\omega t}\bigr),\qquad B(x,t):=\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\widetilde B(x)e^{-i\omega t}\bigr)\qquad((x,t)\in D\times\mathbb R),$$ componentwise, with the complex exponential and real part of [[def-complex-exponential]] and [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]; this is the encoding convention of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]] specialized from plane-wave amplitudes to a general $C^\infty$ amplitude, and the complex fields are not themselves physical fields. (b) [Source-free class] The pair $(\widetilde E,\widetilde B)$ is called a **frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pair on $D$** when it is $C^\infty$ and satisfies, on $D$, $$\operatorname{div}\widetilde E=0,\qquad \operatorname{div}\widetilde B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}\widetilde E=i\omega\widetilde B,\qquad \operatorname{curl}\widetilde B=-i\omega\varepsilon_0\mu_0\widetilde E=-i\omega c^{-2}\widetilde E,$$ with the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] applied componentwise to the complex fields. The word 'source-free' records that the displayed equations carry no charge or current term; the associated real fields are read as an electric and a magnetic field of [[def-em-fields]], $\omega$ is the angular frequency and $T:=2\pi/\omega$ the period. (c) [Status and scope] This item fixes the encoding, the four phasor equations and the terminology only. It asserts no equation for the associated real fields, no outgoing or boundary condition, no existence or uniqueness statement, no energy or flux reading and no empirical content. In particular the deduction that the associated real fields satisfy the smooth-branch vacuum Maxwell equations with zero sources is not part of this definition; for the pairs used on this page it is established by the exterior-scattering theorem recorded later on this page. Only $C^\infty$ pairs on an open set are defined, so no boundary trace, weak or distributional class is introduced here.
items.strategy: This is a definition contract assembled from earlier items; well-definedness is discharged by the cited suppliers. (i) The encoding (a) is the real-part-of-complex-amplitude convention of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]] with a general $C^\infty$ spatial amplitude; the componentwise real part of [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]] and the complex exponential of [[def-complex-exponential]] are total on $\mathbb C^3$, so the associated real fields are defined for every $C^\infty$ pair, with no equation assumed. (ii) The class (b) is cut out by four equations on the open set $D$: the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] act componentwise on the $C^\infty$ complex fields, and the two constants satisfy $\varepsilon_0\mu_0=c^{-2}$ by [[def-em-si-conventions]]; the displayed third and fourth equations use only complex scalar multiplication, so the class is well-defined without any choice principle. (iii) The physical reading of the associated real fields as an electric and a magnetic field uses [[def-em-fields]]; the units of $\widetilde E$ are V$\,$m$^{-1}$ and those of $\widetilde B$ are T, inherited from that definition. (iv) Clause (c) records exactly what is not asserted; in particular the complex Maxwell-to-real-Maxwell deduction is deliberately left to a consumer, because a definition must not assert the field equations of its associated real fields.

items.title: Real parts of $e^{-i\omega t}$ phasors: calculus, injectivity and equivalence with the real Helmholtz-Maxwell system
items.reference: scaffold-added necessary mathematical prerequisite for the vector PEC scattering theorem (see research/physics-em-sr-40-2026-10-08-batch-40.notes.md)
items.statement: Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, $c>0$ and $\omega>0$, and let $\widetilde E,\widetilde B:D\to\mathbb C^3$. Define $E,B:D\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ by $E(x,t):=\operatorname{Re}(\widetilde E(x)e^{-i\omega t})$ and $B(x,t):=\operatorname{Re}(\widetilde B(x)e^{-i\omega t})$ componentwise ([[def-complex-exponential]], [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]; [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]] for the classes). Then: (a) [Calculus] if $\widetilde E,\widetilde B$ are $C^1$, then $E,B$ are $C^1$ and at every $(x,t)\in D\times\mathbb R$: $\partial_tE(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(-i\omega\widetilde E(x)e^{-i\omega t})$, and likewise for $B$; for each $j\in\{1,2,3\}$, $\partial_jE(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(\partial_j\widetilde E(x)e^{-i\omega t})$, and likewise for $B$; and with the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] acting on the spatial variable, $\operatorname{div}E(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}((\operatorname{div}\widetilde E)(x)e^{-i\omega t})$, $\operatorname{curl}E(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}((\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E)(x)e^{-i\omega t})$, and likewise for $B$. (b) [Injectivity] if $w\in\mathbb C^3$ and $\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})=0$ for all $t\in\mathbb R$, then $w=0$; more generally, if $w:D\to\mathbb C^3$ is continuous and $\operatorname{Re}(w(x)e^{-i\omega t})=0$ for all $(x,t)\in D\times\mathbb R$, then $w\equiv0$ on $D$. (c) [Equivalence] if $\widetilde E,\widetilde B$ are $C^1$, the phasor system $$\operatorname{div}\widetilde E=0,\quad\operatorname{div}\widetilde B=0,\quad\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E=i\omega\widetilde B,\quad\operatorname{curl}\widetilde B=-i\omega c^{-2}\widetilde E$$ holds on $D$ if and only if the real system $$\operatorname{div}E=0,\quad\operatorname{div}B=0,\quad\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\quad\operatorname{curl}B=c^{-2}\partial_tE$$ holds on $D\times\mathbb R$.
items.strategy: Write the encoding in real components: by the Cartesian form and Euler identity of [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]], $\operatorname{Re}(w(x)e^{-i\omega t})=(\operatorname{Re}w(x))\cos(\omega t)+(\operatorname{Im}w(x))\sin(\omega t)$ componentwise, with the real and imaginary parts of [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]] and the complex arithmetic of [[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]. (a) For fixed $x$ each component is a constant-coefficient combination of $\cos(\omega t)$ and $\sin(\omega t)$; the affine map $t\mapsto\omega t$ has derivative $\omega$ by [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], and [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]] applied to the differentiable real sine and cosine maps of [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]] gives their composite derivatives. The sum, scalar-multiple and product rules of [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] then give $\partial_tE=\operatorname{Re}(-i\omega\widetilde Ee^{-i\omega t})$, and the spatial derivatives pass through the constant coefficients, giving the spatial formulas for each component; the divergence and curl formulas follow by applying the componentwise formulas and the linearity of [[lem-divergence-and-curl-are-linear-and-obey-the-scalar-product-rules]] (for complex fields, componentwise in real and imaginary parts). (b) Evaluating at $t=0$ gives $\operatorname{Re}w=0$; evaluating at $t=\pi/(2\omega)$ gives $\operatorname{Re}(-iw)=\operatorname{Im}w=0$ by the quarter-turn values of [[thm-quarter-turn-values-and-shift-formulas]] and the Cartesian form of [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]], so $w=0$. The continuous case applies the pointwise result at each $x\in D$; no choice principle is used. (c) Direction (i)$\Rightarrow$(ii): substitute the phasor equations into the calculus formulas of (a); e.g. $\operatorname{curl}E=\operatorname{Re}((\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E)e^{-i\omega t})=\operatorname{Re}(i\omega\widetilde Be^{-i\omega t})=-\partial_tB$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=\operatorname{Re}(-i\omega c^{-2}\widetilde Ee^{-i\omega t})=c^{-2}\partial_tE$. Direction (ii)$\Rightarrow$(i): subtract the complex expressions and apply (b), e.g. $\operatorname{Re}((\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E-i\omega\widetilde B)e^{-i\omega t})=0$ for all $(x,t)$ forces $\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E=i\omega\widetilde B$; the other three equations are analogous. All statements are pointwise algebraic identities; no PDE existence, no boundary condition and no choice principle is used.

items.title: Periodic responses of $\ddot z=\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})$ and the affine classification of all solutions
items.reference: scaffold-added necessary mathematical prerequisite for the weak-field Thomson item (see research/physics-em-sr-40-2026-10-08-batch-40.notes.md)
items.statement: Let $\omega>0$, $T:=2\pi/\omega$, $n\ge1$ and $w\in\mathbb C^n$; use the real part and complex exponential of [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]] and [[def-complex-exponential]]. Define $z_p:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^n$ by $z_p(t):=\operatorname{Re}(-w\omega^{-2}e^{-i\omega t})$ componentwise ([[def-derivative]] for the derivative below). Then: (a) $z_p$ is $C^\infty$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) and satisfies $z_p''(t)=\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$; it is $T$-periodic. (b) every $C^2$ solution $z:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^n$ of $z''(t)=\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})$ on $\mathbb R$ has the form $z(t)=z_p(t)+a+bt$ with unique $a,b\in\mathbb R^n$. (c) such a solution is $T$-periodic if and only if $b=0$; the $T$-periodic solutions are exactly $z_p(t)+a$, $a\in\mathbb R^n$, and their oscillating part has complex amplitude $-w/\omega^2$. (d) [Local solutions and exact global extension] Let I be any nonempty open interval, t* in I, and let z:I->R^n be C2 with the same harmonic equation on I. Then z=z_p+a+bt on I for a UNIQUE pair a,b, with b=z'(t*)-z_p'(t*) and a=z(t*)-z_p(t*)-bt*. The same explicit formula defines its unique global harmonic-ODE extension Z on R. This extension is T-periodic exactly when b0, equivalently z'(t*)=z_p'(t*); when b0 its mean over every complete period is a. For general drift, the mean of its global extension over [t,t+T] is a+b(t+T/2). Thus periodic preparation can be imposed on the global response without requiring a driven nonlinear family to exist on R. If I contains at least one pair t,t+T, equality at that pair forces b0. If I contains no such pair, a condition expressed only as z(t+T)=z(t) wherever both arguments belong to I is vacuous and does not imply periodicity of the global extension. All affine-drift local solutions remain classified, and the original global branches(a)-(c) remain intact.
items.strategy: (a) By the Cartesian form and Euler identity of [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]], $z_p(t)=-\omega^{-2}[(\operatorname{Re}w)\cos(\omega t)+(\operatorname{Im}w)\sin(\omega t)]$ componentwise. Differentiating twice with the sum, scalar-multiple and product rules of [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] and the derivatives of [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]] gives $z_p''=\operatorname{Re}w\cos(\omega t)+\operatorname{Im}w\sin(\omega t)=\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})$. Periodicity of $z_p$ follows from $e^{-i\omega(t+T)}=e^{-i\omega t}e^{-i\omega T}=e^{-i\omega t}$ by the addition law of [[thm-complex-exponential-addition-and-real-extension]] and $e^{-2\pi i}=1$, the latter from the Cartesian form and the values $\cos2\pi=1$, $\sin2\pi=0$ of [[thm-sine-cosine-zero-sets-and-fundamental-period]]. (b) If $z$ is any $C^2$ solution, then $h:=z-z_p$ satisfies $h''=0$ on $\mathbb R$. Apply [[cor-zero-derivative-implies-constant]] on the interval $\mathbb R$ ([[def-interval]]) to each component of $h'$: $h'=b$ is constant. Applying the same corollary to $h-b\,\mathrm{id}$ gives $h=a+bt$, and consequently $z=z_p+a+bt$. Uniqueness of $a,b$ from $z(0)$ and $z'(0)$ is immediate. (c) If $b=0$ then $z=z_p+a$ is $T$-periodic by (a). Conversely, if $z$ is $T$-periodic then $z(t+T)-z(t)=bT$ for all $t$, hence $b=0$; then $z-z_p=a$ is the constant part whose complex amplitude is zero, while the oscillating part $z_p$ has complex amplitude $-w/\omega^2$ by construction. No choice principle is used. For(d), apply the zero-derivative corollary on each closed subinterval of I to h'=z'-z_p', then to h-b id; any two points of the interval are contained in such a subinterval, so the constants agree throughout I. Evaluate at t* to get the displayed a,b, proving uniqueness. The explicit global formula is a solution on R by(a), and every other global solution extending z has the same value and derivative at t*, hence the same affine constants. Its period increment is bT, giving the periodicity equivalences and the single-pair test. Over every interval [t,t+T] the harmonic sine/cosine part has mean zero by scalar FTC. The affine part a+b s has mean a+b(t+T/2), since its integral is aT+b[(t+T)²-t²]/2. Therefore the global extension z_p+a+b s has mean a+b(t+T/2); it has mean a over EVERY complete period if and only if b=0. This last claim uses only ordinary finite-period integrals and no choice. The derivatives in(a) use the total chain rule [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]] componentwise (or scalar coordinate-line chain rules), not a derivative rule asserted by the exponential definition alone.

items.title: The ideal harmonic electric-dipole radiation model
items.reference: scaffold-added necessary model definition for the dipole scattering and Thomson items (see research/physics-em-sr-40-2026-10-08-batch-40.notes.md)
items.statement: Let $\omega>0$, $k:=\omega/c$ with $c$ the vacuum speed of [[def-em-si-conventions]], $\mu_0>0$ the vacuum permeability of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and $p_0\in\mathbb C^3$ (the complex dipole-moment amplitude, in $\mathrm C\,\mathrm m$). Define, on the punctured space $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ and all times $t\in\mathbb R$, $$E_{\rm d}(x,t):=\operatorname{Re}\Bigl(-\frac{\mu_0\omega^2}{4\pi r}\,n\times(n\times p_0)\,e^{i(kr-\omega t)}\Bigr),\qquad B_{\rm d}(x,t):=\frac1c\,n\times E_{\rm d}(x,t),$$ where $r:=|x|$ and $n:=x/r$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]), with the real part and complex exponential of [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]] and [[def-complex-exponential]] and the componentwise real-part encoding convention of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]] (the spatial amplitude here varies with x; no plane-wave instance is asserted). Call $(E_{\rm d},B_{\rm d})$ the **ideal harmonic electric-dipole radiation model of frequency $\omega$ and amplitude $p_0$**, and call $S_{\rm d}:=E_{\rm d}\times B_{\rm d}/\mu_0$ its model flux ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]]); the model fields are read as an electric and a magnetic field of [[def-em-fields]]. [Adopted status] This is an explicitly adopted ideal radiation-law model, fixed by the following declarations: (i) it is the leading transverse far-zone field of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]](c) evaluated at the harmonic transverse moment $V(u)=\operatorname{Re}(-\omega^2p_0e^{-i\omega u})$, i.e. at $p''$ for the waveform $p(u)=\operatorname{Re}(p_0e^{-i\omega u})$; (ii) the model contains no independent magnetic-dipole or higher-multipole radiation, no near-zone or static field and no other radiating component; (iii) it is not asserted to solve the vacuum Maxwell equations at finite $r$, to be the field of any actual source, to satisfy any boundary condition or to have finite total energy on $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$; (iv) for compact smooth conserved sources, comparison with these prescribed model fields uses the actual source's moment p_act(u), the harmonic waveform p_h(u)=Re(p0 exp(-i omega u)), their second-derivative mismatch M(u)=|p_act''(u)-p_h''(u)|, and the explicit D,Gamma bounds of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]]. A bound depending only on that source's D and Gamma is valid when M0 on the observation window; the source's moment is not automatically the independently prescribed p0. These actual-source comparison uses assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) carried by the cited theorem. The explicit ideal fields themselves and their pointwise flux definition remain choice-free. No measured, empirical or material-response content is adopted: $p_0$ is prescribed model data, not a derived polarizability.
items.strategy: This is a definition contract; well-definedness is discharged by the cited suppliers. (i) The formula is the leading transverse term $E_{\rm lead}=\mu_0n\times(n\times V)/(4\pi r)$ of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]](c) at $V(u)=\operatorname{Re}(-\omega^2p_0e^{-i\omega u})$: since $p''(u)=\operatorname{Re}(-\omega^2p_0e^{-i\omega u})$ for $p(u)=\operatorname{Re}(p_0e^{-i\omega u})$, the derivative supplied by [[lem-em-harmonic-forcing-periodic-response]](a) with w=-omega²p0, using its explicit C-infinity real harmonic waveform, the model field is exactly $E_{\rm lead}$ rewritten with $u=t-r/c$ and $e^{i(kr-\omega t)}=e^{-i\omega(t-r/c)}$; the cross product, inner product and norm are those of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]] and [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. (ii) $r>0$ on the declared domain, so $E_{\rm d}$ and $B_{\rm d}$ are $C^\infty$ there and the same componentwise real-part convention as [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]] is used; the varying radial amplitude is not a plane-wave amplitude; $E_{\rm d}\cdot n=0$ because $n\times(n\times p_0)$ is orthogonal to $n$, and $B_{\rm d}=n\times E_{\rm d}/c$ by definition. (iii) The model flux $S_{\rm d}$ is the quantity of [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]] evaluated at the model fields; that definition applies to any pair of fields of the declared regularity and assigns no field equation. (iv) The status clause lists the model assumptions (i)-(iv) and excludes exact Maxwell, source-realization, boundary, finite-energy and empirical claims; the model's relation to actual sources is only through the explicit bounds of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]], which are quantified in the item below. The explicit formula/flux construction uses no choice. Actual compact-source comparisons retain the stated Countable Choice of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]], including a moment-mismatch term; no comparison to an arbitrary unrelated harmonic amplitude follows from D alone. Smoothness off r0 follows by coordinate sum/product/chain rules and the positive square-root/reciprocal powers of [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]] for r=|x|; The harmonic lemma supplies all derivatives of the real waveform; compose its second derivative with u=t-r/c using the declared total chain rule. No complex-to-real derivative theorem is silently substituted for that real-waveform interface. Orthogonality is the finite cross-product identity of [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]] applied separately to real and imaginary components. The ideal model is meaningful also at p0=0, giving zero fields; no actual source realization or finite-radius Maxwell equation is deduced.

items.title: Adopted scalar aperture-diffraction model (polarization-insensitive regime)
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]] and [[lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation]] ([[def-countable-choice]]); the smooth modal full-Choice branch of the latter is not used. Adopt as a model assumption of the framework the following scalar aperture-diffraction model. [Data] Fix an angular frequency $\omega>0$ and wavenumber $k:=\omega/c$, with $c$ the vacuum speed of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; let $S\subset\{y\in\mathbb R^3:y_3=0\}\cap\{y:|y|\le a\}$ be a nonempty compact subset of a declared aperture plane $y_3=0$ with aperture radius $a>0$ (the screening plane and spatial region are read in the laboratory chart of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]), and let $\alpha$ be a finite complex measure on $\mathbb R^3$ supported in $S$ (the **aperture distribution**), with $\alpha$ read in volts so that the model field below carries the unit $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$ of an electric-field component and its pairings are those of [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]]. [Model field] The model assigns to every observation point $x$ with $x_3>0$ the complex scalar amplitude $$u(x):=\int G_k(x-y)\,d\alpha(y),$$ where $G_k(z)=e^{ik|z|}/(4\pi|z|)$ for $z\ne0$ is the outgoing Helmholtz kernel of [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]], together with the real scalar field $U(x,t):=\operatorname{Re}(u(x)e^{-i\omega t})$ and the model period-averaged squared field $(1/2)|u(x)|^2$. All model predictions are declared comparisons of this squared field between observation points; no absolute radiometric power or intensity calibration is adopted. [Adopted regime and status] The model is the declared polarization-insensitive scalar approximation of aperture diffraction. It ignores the vector nature and polarization of the electromagnetic field, takes the aperture distribution rather than the exact screen traces as its datum, assigns no back-reaction of the diffracted field on the illumination and no screen interaction beyond the aperture, and is not derived from either branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] or from the material-closure branches of [[post-em-material-closure]]; it is a declared optical approximation, not an exact electromagnetic model. It does not assert that $u$ or $U$ satisfies the Maxwell equations exactly, and it does not identify $\alpha$ with the unknown exact Maxwell boundary traces: assigning both $u$ and $\partial_nu$ on the aperture independently is not a well-posed exact boundary problem, as recorded in [[lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation]], and the error terms of [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]] are the controlled content of the model. No measured intensity, apparatus, sampling model, uncertainty budget, empirical comparison or quantitative radiometric calibration is adopted.
items.strategy: This is an explicit adopted-assumption contract; it is deliberately not a derivation. (i) The mathematical object it adopts is the outgoing source field $u=G_k*\alpha$ of [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]], whose kernel and outgoing/Fraunhofer technique are fixed there. This model permits the compact closed-radius support $|y|\le a$, including aperture corners. Its integral and off-support regularity fall under that supplier by choosing any containing open ball of radius $A>a$; the sharp-radius estimates at $r\ge2a$ are proved directly in the consuming diffraction theorem, so this extension does not evaluate an open-support hypothesis at a boundary point; the integral against the finite complex measure is that of [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]]. (ii) The physical reading uses the aperture plane and spatial region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], the wavenumber-frequency relation $k=\omega/c$ and the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. (iii) The non-derivation clause is essential: neither the smooth nor the weak branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] implies this scalar source model, and the finite-conductivity/material branches of [[post-em-material-closure]] contain no ideal aperture or screen model; the trace caveat is the one recorded in [[lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation]]. (iv) The scope sentences exclude exact Maxwell, vector, polarization, back-reaction, absolute-radiometric and empirical content. The item uses no choice principle beyond those carried by the cited mathematical suppliers (the kernel lemma carries Countable Choice, as stated there). The Countable Choice hypothesis is inherited verbatim from the cited kernel and boundary-representation suppliers; this postulate adds no choice use of its own.

items.physical_scope: Adopted scalar aperture-diffraction model: a finite complex aperture distribution $\alpha$ on a compact planar aperture, the outgoing scalar Helmholtz field $u=G_k*\alpha$, its real-field reading $U=\operatorname{Re}(ue^{-i\omega t})$ and the squared-field comparisons $(1/2)|u|^2$ between observation points, in a declared polarization-insensitive regime. Excluded: derivation from the vacuum Maxwell or material-closure postulates, exact Maxwell validity, identification of $\alpha$ with the exact screen boundary traces, well-posedness of simultaneously prescribed $u$ and $\partial_nu$, polarization and vector effects, aperture back-reaction, absolute radiometric calibration, apparatus, sampling and every empirical comparison.

items.title: Controlled scalar aperture diffraction: Fresnel and Fraunhofer approximations with explicit error terms
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]] and [[lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation]] ([[def-countable-choice]]), whose trace qualification is used in clause (d); the full-Choice modal branch of the latter is not used. Adopt the scalar aperture model and its notation from [[post-em-scalar-aperture-model]]: frequency $\omega>0$, $k=\omega/c$, aperture radius $a>0$, finite complex aperture distribution $\alpha$ supported in the planar aperture $S\subset\{y_3=0\}\cap\{y:|y|\le a\}$, model field $u=G_k*\alpha$, real field $U(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(u(x)e^{-i\omega t})$ and $T=2\pi/\omega$ ([[def-em-si-conventions]], [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-complex-exponential]], [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]], [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]]). Set $I(x):=(1/2)|u(x)|^2$. Then: (a) [Model field and Fraunhofer estimate] $u$ is $C^\infty$ on the half-space $\{x_3>0\}$ and on $\mathbb R^3\setminus S$, satisfies $(\Delta+k^2)u=0$ there, and is outgoing in the sense of [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]]: for $x=rn$ with $r\ge2a$ and $n\in S^2$, $$u(rn)=\frac{e^{ikr}}{4\pi r}\int e^{-ikn\cdot y}\,d\alpha(y)+O\Bigl(\frac{\|\alpha\|_{\rm TV}}{r}\Bigl[\frac ar+\frac{ka^2}{r}\Bigr]\Bigr)$$ uniformly in direction, and $r(\partial_ru-iku)=O(r^{-1})$ uniformly. (b) [Fresnel estimate] write $y_t=(y_1,y_2)$ and $\xi=(\xi_1,\xi_2)$ for transverse vectors; for the planar aperture and observation $x=(\xi_1,\xi_2,z)$ with $z>0$, $b\ge0$, $|\xi|\le b$ and any declared fixed small-angle range $(a+b)/z\le\eta_0<1$, where $0<\eta_0<1$, the Fresnel approximation replaces $R=|x-y|$ by $z+|\xi-y_t|^2/(2z)$ and $1/R$ by $1/z$ in the model integral with phase error $O(k(a+b)^4/z^3)$, relative amplitude error $O((a+b)^2/z^2)$ and absolute field error $O(\|\alpha\|_{\rm TV}z^{-1}[(a+b)^2/z^2+k(a+b)^4/z^3])$. (c) [Intensity and error transfer] at every $x$ with $x_3>0$ the model period average satisfies $\frac1T\int_0^TU(x,s)^2\,ds=I(x)$ ([[lem-em-period-average]]). If $u_{\rm approx}$ is any approximation of $u$ with $|u_{\rm approx}(x)-u(x)|\le\delta(x)$, then $|\frac12|u_{\rm approx}(x)|^2-I(x)|\le\frac12\delta(x)(|u(x)|+|u_{\rm approx}(x)|)$; if moreover $u(x)\ne0$ and $|u_{\rm approx}(x)-u(x)|\le\epsilon(x)|u(x)|$, the relative intensity error is at most $2\epsilon(x)+\epsilon(x)^2$. In particular the Fraunhofer and Fresnel field errors of (a) and (b) bound the corresponding intensity errors; no new approximation is introduced by passing to $I$. (d) [Trace and scope] the aperture distribution $\alpha$ is an adopted model datum and is not identified with the exact Maxwell boundary data on the screen; assigning both $u$ and $\partial_nu$ on the aperture independently does not produce a well-posed exact boundary problem ([[lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation]]). The construction ignores polarization and aperture back-reaction, makes no claim that $u$ or $U$ satisfies the Maxwell equations exactly, and makes no measured-intensity, apparatus, sampling or empirical claim; only comparisons of $I$ between observation points are read as model predictions.
items.strategy: The theorem instantiates the mathematical field estimates of [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]] at the adopted model datum of [[post-em-scalar-aperture-model]]. (a) The model field is the supplier's convolution. Choose any open containing ball of radius $A>a$ to obtain its off-support smoothness and Helmholtz equation. For the advertised sharp-radius endpoint, argue directly for every $|y|\le a$ and $r\ge2a$. Write $R=|rn-y|$, so $R\ge r-a\ge r/2$. For $h(s)=|rn-sy|$, the exact norm derivative formula from the supplier gives $|h''(s)|\le2a^2/(r-a)\le4a^2/r$; twice FTC therefore gives $|R-r+n\cdot y|\le2a^2/r$, and $|r/R-1|\le2a/r$. The supplier's real phase bound $|e^{i\theta}-1|\le|\theta|$ now gives $$\left|G_k(rn-y)-\frac{e^{ikr}e^{-ikn\cdot y}}{4\pi r}\right|\le\frac1{2\pi r}\left(\frac ar+\frac{ka^2}r\right).$$ For a bounded continuous kernel $f$ on the compact support, $|\int f\,d\alpha|\le\sup|f|\,\|\alpha\|_{\rm TV}$ follows by [[prop-simple-integrals-are-bounded-by-total-variation]] and uniform finite-simple approximation in [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]]; hence this pointwise bound proves the original field error, including $r=2a$. The exact derivative $\partial_rR=(r-n\cdot y)/R$ has modulus at most1 and $|\partial_rR-1|\le2a^2/r^2$. Differentiating the explicit kernel gives $r|\partial_rG_k-ikG_k|\le(\pi r)^{-1}(1+ka^2/r)$; the same finite-measure bound gives the uniform outgoing residual. All derivative passages under the source integral use the supplier's compact-product uniform difference-quotient argument, not an unsupported complex-measure dominated-convergence claim. (b) On the explicitly declared range put $d_0=a+b$ and $s=|\xi-y_t|^2/z^2\le\eta_0^2<1$. The actual supplier proof gives $|\sqrt{1+s}-1-s/2|\le s^2/8$ and $|(1+s)^{-1/2}-1|\le s/2$ by twice FTC. Consequently the phase error is at most $kd_0^4/(8z^3)$ and the relative amplitude error at most $d_0^2/(2z^2)$. The complex-measure kernel bound above gives $$|u-u_{\rm Fresnel}|\le\frac{\|\alpha\|_{\rm TV}}{4\pi z}\left[\frac{d_0^2}{2z^2}+\frac{kd_0^4}{8z^3}\right],$$ which preserves and quantifies all original Fresnel estimates for the closed-support datum. (c) applies [[lem-em-period-average]] with $a=d=u(x)$: $\operatorname{Re}(u(x)e^{-i\omega t})^2$ averages to $\frac12\operatorname{Re}(u(x)\overline{u(x)})=\frac12|u(x)|^2$. The first error bound is the identity $\frac12\bigl||u_{\rm approx}|^2-|u|^2\bigr|=\frac12\bigl||u_{\rm approx}|-|u|\bigr|(|u_{\rm approx}|+|u|)$ together with $\bigl||u_{\rm approx}|-|u|\bigr|\le|u_{\rm approx}-u|$, obtained by applying the triangle inequality of [[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]] in both directions; the relative bound is $||u_{\rm approx}|^2-|u|^2|/|u|^2\le\epsilon(2+\epsilon)$. No choice principle beyond that carried by the suppliers is used. (d) reproduces the trace distinction of [[lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation]] and the model-scope declarations of the postulate; the intensity reading is the declared one, so no radiometric claim is added. The Countable Choice hypothesis is inherited from the cited suppliers; the intensity computation of (c) uses only the choice-free period-average lemma.

items.title: Monochromatic scattering by a smooth perfect-electric-conductor obstacle
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as carried by [[lem-em-exterior-vector-helmholtz-mixed-boundary-existence]], whose variational, Sobolev-compactness and compact-spectral steps use it; the algebraic computations below use no further choice. Let $O\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded open set with $C^\infty$ boundary, $D:=\mathbb R^3\setminus\overline O$ connected, $k>0$, $\omega:=ck$ with $c$ the vacuum speed of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and $R>0$ with $\overline O\subset B_R(0)$; let $V\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open with $\overline D\subseteq V$, and let $(\widetilde E_{\rm inc},\widetilde B_{\rm inc})$ be a $C^\infty$ frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pair on $V$ ([[def-em-monochromatic-source-free-phasors]], [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-fields]], [[def-em-si-conventions]]). Plane-wave instances are provided by [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]]: if $\kappa\cdot e=0$, $b=\kappa\times e/\omega$ and $|\kappa|=\omega/c$, then $(\widetilde E_{\rm inc},\widetilde B_{\rm inc})(x)=(e\,e^{i\kappa\cdot x},b\,e^{i\kappa\cdot x})$ satisfies the four phasor equations on $\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-em-plane-wave-definition]]). Adopt the ideal perfectly conducting (PEC) boundary model: the tangential component of the total electric field vanishes on $\partial O$. This is a declared idealization of the stationary interface conditions of [[pthm-em-material-stationary-jumps]] with vanishing fields inside the conductor; it is not one of the finite-conductivity branches of [[post-em-material-closure]], and the induced surface charge and current are neither prescribed nor determined here. Let $e_T$ be the tangential projection of $-\widetilde E_{\rm inc}$ on $\partial O$, and let $\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$ be the unique $C^\infty$ field on $\overline D$ of [[lem-em-exterior-vector-helmholtz-mixed-boundary-existence]] with $(\Delta+k^2)\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=0$ and $\operatorname{div}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=0$ on $D$ ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]), tangential trace $e_T$ on $\partial O$ and that lemma's outgoing modal condition on $S_R$. Set $\widetilde B_{\rm scat}:=(i\omega)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$ and, on $D$, $\widetilde E_{\rm tot}:=\widetilde E_{\rm inc}+\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$, $\widetilde B_{\rm tot}:=\widetilde B_{\rm inc}+\widetilde B_{\rm scat}$. Then: (a) [Phasor Maxwell] $(\widetilde E_{\rm scat},\widetilde B_{\rm scat})$ and $(\widetilde E_{\rm tot},\widetilde B_{\rm tot})$ are $C^\infty$ frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pairs on $D$; and for every $C^\infty$ frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pair $(\widetilde E,\widetilde B)$ on an open set $O'\subseteq\mathbb R^3$, the associated real fields of [[def-em-monochromatic-source-free-phasors]] satisfy on $O'\times\mathbb R$ the smooth-branch vacuum Maxwell equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] with $\rho\equiv0$ and $J\equiv0$. Consequently the associated real total fields $E_{\rm tot},B_{\rm tot}$ satisfy those source-free equations on $D\times\mathbb R$. (b) [PEC boundary condition] the tangential trace of $\widetilde E_{\rm tot}$ on $\partial O$ vanishes; hence for every unit normal field $n$ of $\partial O$ the associated real total electric field $E_{\rm tot}(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(\widetilde E_{\rm tot}(x)e^{-i\omega t})$ ([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]) satisfies $n\times E_{\rm tot}=0$ on $\partial O\times\mathbb R$. (c) [Uniqueness] if $(\widetilde E',\widetilde B')$ is a $C^\infty$ frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pair on an open set $V'\supseteq\overline D$ that is outgoing on $S_R$ in the modal sense of the vector Helmholtz lemma and has tangential trace $e_T$ on $\partial O$, then $(\widetilde E',\widetilde B')=(\widetilde E_{\rm scat},\widetilde B_{\rm scat})$ on $D$; equivalently $(\widetilde E_{\rm tot},\widetilde B_{\rm tot})$ is the unique total source-free phasor pair in the corresponding $C^\infty$ closure class with that prescribed incident phasor, vanishing tangential electric trace, and outgoing scattered correction $\widetilde E_{\rm tot}-\widetilde E_{\rm inc}$ in the lemma's modal class. The total field itself is not required to be outgoing; an incident plane wave is generally not outgoing. (d) [Scope] one positive frequency $\omega=ck$, one smooth bounded stationary PEC obstacle with connected exterior, and $C^\infty$ incident and scattered classes only; no lossy, impedance, nonsmooth or dispersive obstacle, no determination of the induced surface charge or current, no radiation-zone amplitude or far-field asymptotics beyond the lemma's outgoing modal class, no point or singular source, no finite-energy or empirical claim.
items.strategy: Assume the Axiom of Choice exactly through [[lem-em-exterior-vector-helmholtz-mixed-boundary-existence]] (its symmetry/coercivity, compactness and compact-spectral steps); all other steps are pointwise algebra. (a) For the scattered pair: $\operatorname{div}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=0$ is the boundary-problem condition; $\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=i\omega\widetilde B_{\rm scat}$ holds by the definition of $\widetilde B_{\rm scat}$; $\operatorname{div}\widetilde B_{\rm scat}=(i\omega)^{-1}\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E_{\rm scat})=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}\widetilde B_{\rm scat}=(i\omega)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}(\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E_{\rm scat})=(i\omega)^{-1}(\nabla\operatorname{div}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}-\Delta\widetilde E_{\rm scat})=(i\omega)^{-1}k^2\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=-i\omega c^{-2}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$ by [[cor-the-curl-of-a-curl-of-a-c2-field]], [[thm-the-divergence-of-a-curl-vanishes]] and $(\Delta+k^2)\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=0$; the sum of two solutions of the linear system is a solution by [[lem-divergence-and-curl-are-linear-and-obey-the-scalar-product-rules]]. The real-field Maxwell statement is clause (c) of [[lem-em-phasor-real-part-calculus-and-equivalence]] with the constant $c$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]], combined with the identification of its real system with the zero-source smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]; the incident pair is a pair on $V$, hence on $D$. (b) The tangential traces satisfy $\widetilde E_{\rm tot,tang}=\widetilde E_{\rm inc,tang}+\widetilde E_{\rm scat,tang}=\widetilde E_{\rm inc,tang}+e_T=0$ on $\partial O$; the associated real field is the real part of the tangential trace, hence vanishes (the encoding and real-part calculus are those of [[def-em-monochromatic-source-free-phasors]] and [[lem-em-phasor-real-part-calculus-and-equivalence]]). (c) For a candidate phasor pair, $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E'=i\omega\operatorname{curl}\widetilde B'=\omega^2c^{-2}\widetilde E'=k^2\widetilde E'$, and $\operatorname{div}\widetilde E'=0$. The componentwise real/imaginary curl-curl identity thus gives $(\Delta+k^2)\widetilde E'=0$. Its prescribed tangential trace and outgoing correction are the declared boundary class. Hence the candidate $\widetilde E'$ satisfies all hypotheses of the uniqueness assertion of [[lem-em-exterior-vector-helmholtz-mixed-boundary-existence]] for the same tangential data, so $\widetilde E'=\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$; then $\widetilde B'=(i\omega)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E'=(i\omega)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=\widetilde B_{\rm scat}$ by the third phasor equation of [[def-em-monochromatic-source-free-phasors]]. For the total-field formulation subtract the fixed incident pair: linearity gives a source-free correction with tangential trace $e_T$, and the required outgoing condition is on that correction. Conversely adding the fixed incident pair recovers the total boundary condition. Thus uniqueness transfers exactly to total-minus-incident outgoing; it does not impose the outgoing class on an incident plane wave or on their total. (d) records the exact scope; in particular the ideal PEC condition is adopted, not derived, and the material-closure branches of [[post-em-material-closure]] contain no $\sigma\to\infty$ branch, while [[pthm-em-material-stationary-jumps]] supplies only the stationary-interface idealization context.

items.title: Differential and total cross sections of the ideal harmonic dipole in a plane-wave field
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]] and [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]] ([[def-countable-choice]]); the period-average and cross-section algebra itself uses no choice. Adopt the ideal harmonic electric-dipole radiation model of [[def-em-ideal-harmonic-dipole-model]] with frequency $\omega>0$, wavenumber $k=\omega/c$ and amplitude $p_0\in\mathbb C^3$; let $E_{\rm d},B_{\rm d},S_{\rm d}$ be its fields and model flux. Let $\kappa\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ with $|\kappa|=\omega/c$, $e\in\mathbb C^3\setminus\{0\}$ with $\kappa\cdot e=0$, $b:=\kappa\times e/\omega$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), and let $(E_{\rm inc},B_{\rm inc})$ be the corresponding plane-wave fields of [[def-em-plane-wave-definition]] on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$; by [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]] they satisfy the smooth-branch source-free vacuum Maxwell equations, and by [[pthm-em-wave-energy-average]](b) their period-averaged energy flux has magnitude $I_{\rm inc}=\frac{\varepsilon_0c}{2}|e|^2=\frac{|e|^2}{2\mu_0c}$ ([[def-em-si-conventions]]). Define the **model differential scattering cross section** by $$\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}(n):=\frac{r^2\langle S_{\rm d}(rn,\cdot)\cdot n\rangle}{\langle S_{\rm inc}\cdot\hat\kappa\rangle},\qquad n\in S^2,\ r>0,$$ where $\hat\kappa:=\kappa/|\kappa|$, $S_{\rm inc}:=E_{\rm inc}\times B_{\rm inc}/\mu_0$ ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]]), and $\langle f\rangle:=\frac1T\int_0^Tf(s)\,ds$, $T=2\pi/\omega$, is the period average at fixed observation point. Then: (a) [Angular pattern] the ratio is independent of $r$ and of the averaging start, and for every $n\in S^2$ $$\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}(n)=\frac{\omega^4|n\times p_0|^2}{16\pi^2\varepsilon_0^2c^4|e|^2}=\frac{\mu_0^2\omega^4|n\times p_0|^2}{16\pi^2|e|^2}.$$ (b) [Total cross section] with $d\sigma_{S^2}$ the surface measure of the unit sphere, $\sigma:=\int_{S^2}\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}\,d\sigma_{S^2}$ equals $$\sigma=\frac{\omega^4|p_0|^2}{6\pi\varepsilon_0^2c^4|e|^2}=\frac{\mu_0^2\omega^4|p_0|^2}{6\pi|e|^2};$$ if $p_0=\alpha e$ for a complex scalar $\alpha$ (the scalar polarizability, in $\mathrm F\,\mathrm m^2$), then $\sigma=\frac{\omega^4|\alpha|^2}{6\pi\varepsilon_0^2c^4}$ and $\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}(n)=\frac{\omega^4|\alpha|^2}{16\pi^2\varepsilon_0^2c^4}|n\times\hat e|^2$ with $\hat e:=e/|e|$. (c) [Fidelity for arbitrary actual sources and matched windows] Let an actual compact smooth conserved source satisfy the exact hypotheses of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]], with spatial support radius a>0, source-time interval [tau0,tau1], moment p_act(u), variation bound D(u) and constants Gamma_E,Gamma_B. These source data are independent of the prescribed model amplitude p0. Put
$$p_h(u):=\operatorname{Re}(p_0e^{-i\omega u}),\qquad M(u):=|p_{\rm act}''(u)-p_h''(u)|.$$
For n in S2,u in[tau0,tau1],r>=2a, define
$$H(u,r):=\frac{\Gamma_E}{r^2}+\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi r}[D(u)+M(u)].$$
The actual retarded fields and the model fields satisfy, uniformly in n,
$$|E_{\rm act}(rn,u+r/c)-E_{\rm d}(rn,u+r/c)|\le H(u,r),$$
$$|B_{\rm act}(rn,u+r/c)-B_{\rm d}(rn,u+r/c)|\le\frac{\Gamma_B+\Gamma_E/c}{r^2}+\frac{H(u,r)}c.$$
Also retain the sharper direct source-leading-field consequence
$$|B_{\rm act}-B_{\rm d}|\le\frac{\Gamma_B}{r^2}+\frac{\mu_0[D(u)+M(u)]}{4\pi cr}$$
at the same events. If p_act''=p_h'' on a specified finite window, M0 there and these give the full matched dipole bounds; in particular they imply the older coarser electric bound Gamma_E/r²+mu0 D/(2pi r). Neither moment matching nor D0 is automatic. A sound sufficient matched branch is p_act=p_h+a0+b0 u on an open neighborhood of the window (any fixed real vectors a0,b0). Such a branch has actual compact realizations over any finite window: choose a smooth time cutoff eta equal1 near the window, let p_eta=eta(p_h+a0+b0 u), choose a nonnegative smooth spatial bump sigma with support inside B_a and integral1, and set rho=-p_eta dot grad sigma,J=p_eta' sigma. Then continuity holds and the actual moment is p_eta; outside the window it is tapered. Apply the actual theorem with the resulting D and Gamma, retaining every finite-radius/source-variation error. No eternal harmonic moment of a compact-time source is asserted. (d) [Scope] conditional predictions of the adopted ideal model: no measured cross section, no frequency-domain response law (the amplitude $p_0$ is prescribed model data), no magnetic-dipole or higher-multipole content, no self-force, material response, finite-size or empirical claim; the scalar-$\alpha$ clause records a declared proportional response, not a derived polarizability. In all complex-amplitude formulas |v|²=sum_i |v_i|² is the Hermitian norm square; n cross v is complex-linear for real n. The p0=0 case gives zero scattered fields and cross sections while the nonzero incident intensity still defines the ratios. Actual-source fidelity assumes only the explicitly quantified mismatch and source hypotheses; it does not turn the model cross section into a measured or self-consistent scattering prediction.
items.strategy: (a) In the model, $B_{\rm d}=n\times E_{\rm d}/c$ and $n\cdot E_{\rm d}=0$, so $S_{\rm d}\cdot n=n\cdot(E_{\rm d}\times(n\times E_{\rm d}))/(\mu_0c)=|E_{\rm d}|^2/(\mu_0c)$ pointwise; writing $w:=-\frac{\mu_0\omega^2}{4\pi r}n\times(n\times p_0)e^{ikr}$, the model has $E_{\rm d}=\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})$, and [[lem-em-period-average]] gives $\langle|E_{\rm d}|^2\rangle=\frac12|w|^2=\frac{\mu_0^2\omega^4}{32\pi^2r^2}|n\times p_0|^2$ ([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]], [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]]). Hence $r^2\langle S_{\rm d}\cdot n\rangle=\frac{\mu_0\omega^4}{32\pi^2c}|n\times p_0|^2$, independent of $r$ and of the averaging start. Division by the incident flux $I_{\rm inc}=\frac{|e|^2}{2\mu_0c}$ of [[pthm-em-wave-energy-average]](b) and $\mu_0^2=\frac1{\varepsilon_0^2c^4}$ ([[def-em-si-conventions]]) give the two displayed forms. (b) [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]](d) gives $\int_{S^2}|n\times a|^2d\sigma=\frac{8\pi}3|a|^2$ for real $a$, and applying it to the real and imaginary parts of $p_0$ gives the complex case; integrating the pattern of (a) over $S^2$ yields $\frac{\mu_0^2\omega^4}{16\pi^2|e|^2}\cdot\frac{8\pi}3|p_0|^2=\frac{\mu_0^2\omega^4|p_0|^2}{6\pi|e|^2}$, i.e. the two displayed forms. For $p_0=\alpha e$ substitute $|p_0|^2=|\alpha|^2|e|^2$ and $|n\times p_0|^2=|\alpha|^2|e|^2|n\times\hat e|^2$ ([[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]]). (c) At t=u+r/c the SIGNED model leading field is mu0 n cross(n cross p_h''(u))/(4pi r). The actual source theorem bounds E_act against the leading field of p_act'' by Gamma_E/r²+mu0 D/(4pi r). The real unit-direction double-cross projection has norm at most1, so the difference of the two leading fields is bounded by mu0 M/(4pi r). Adding gives H, including the zero actual source countercheck: then D=Gamma0 but M=|p_h''|, which exactly accounts for a nonzero prescribed model. The source theorem's B-n cross E_act/c bound is (Gamma_B+Gamma_E/c)/r²; add c^-1 times H to obtain the retained magnetic bound. Separately its stronger B-leading(V_act) estimate is Gamma_B/r²; |V_act-p_h''|<=D+M gives the sharper direct magnetic estimate. For the compact-window construction, smooth nonnegative cutoffs from [[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]] may be normalized and scaled to give sigma ([[def-mollifier-family-generated-by-a-unit-mass-smooth-bump]] for the scaling convention). Continuity is rho_t=-p_eta' dot grad sigma and div J=p_eta' dot grad sigma. Integration by parts on a bounding rectangle gives integral rho0 and integral y_i rho=(p_eta)_i integral sigma=(p_eta)_i, using [[thm-integration-by-parts]], [[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]] and the Countable-Choice comparison [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]]. Choose source-time endpoints outside the taper support, so all compact smooth hypotheses are met. Moment matching on the window removes M, but D and Gamma remain the actual finite-source quantities. (d) records the scope; no measured or material content is added ([[def-em-si-conventions]] only fixes units and constants). No choice principle beyond that carried by [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]] and [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]] (Countable Choice, as stated there) is used. The Countable Choice hypothesis is inherited from the actual compact-source and sphere-moment suppliers; the finite period-average calculation and cross-section algebra are choice-free. Complex norms mean |v|²=sum_i |v_i|². Real unit n acts complex-linearly by cross products; all norm identities used in(a),(b) follow by summing the real and imaginary norm identities. The minus sign in w agrees with the model definition; squaring for its flux does not erase a sign mismatch in the field identity. Period averaging adds no choice; Countable Choice here is precisely the actual source/sphere-integral premise.

items.title: Controlled first variation of the relativistic test-charge law: the leading Thomson-model cross section
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by [[pthm-em-dipole-scattering-cross-section]]; the linearization below and [[lem-em-harmonic-forcing-periodic-response]] use no choice. Assume the setting and postulates of [[pthm-em-relativistic-lorentz-force]] for a test particle with charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$ ([[def-em-sources]](a)) and externally supplied rest mass $m>0$, in the incident plane-wave field of [[def-em-plane-wave-definition]] with wavevector $\kappa$, complex amplitude $e\ne0$, $\kappa\cdot e=0$, $|\kappa|=\omega/c$ and $b=\kappa\times e/\omega$ as in [[pthm-em-dipole-scattering-cross-section]]; write $E_{\rm inc}(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(e\,e^{i(\kappa\cdot x-\omega t)})$ and $B_{\rm inc}=\kappa\times E_{\rm inc}/\omega$ ([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]], [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-si-conventions]]). Assume that for some $\eta_0>0$ and a common open interval $I\ni0$, for every $\eta\in(-\eta_0,\eta_0)$ there is a $C^2$ future timelike massive solution $r_\eta:I\to\mathbb R^3$ of the adopted four-force law in the external field $\eta(E_{\rm inc},B_{\rm inc})$ (no self-field, recoil or material force), and that the family admits a uniform first-order expansion: there are $r_1\in C^2(I;\mathbb R^3)$ and, for every compact $K\subset I$, a constant $C_K$ with $$|r_\eta(t)-x_0-\eta r_1(t)|+|\dot r_\eta(t)-\eta\dot r_1(t)|\le C_K\eta^2\qquad(t\in K,\ |\eta|<\eta_0)$$ about a fixed position $x_0\in\mathbb R^3$, The family time interval I is not required to contain a full period, and no solution r_eta outside I is assumed. For the periodic-response conclusions(b),(c), impose the following explicit preparation(P): the unique global harmonic-ODE extension of r1 supplied after(a) by [[lem-em-harmonic-forcing-periodic-response]](d), with its actual value and derivative at0, is T-periodic, T=2pi/omega. Equivalently its affine drift is zero, or $r_1'(0)=\operatorname{Re}(iw/\omega)$ with $w=(q/m)e e^{i\kappa\cdot x_0}$. The linearized equation and affine local/global classification in(a) hold for every stated family even without(P); overlap-only periodicity on a short I is not substituted for(P). Then: (a) [Linearized equation] $\ddot r_1(t)=\frac qmE_{\rm inc}(x_0,t)=\frac qm\operatorname{Re}(e\,e^{i(\kappa\cdot x_0-\omega t)})$ on $I$. (b) [Induced dipole under preparation(P)] $x_0$ is the zeroth-order rest/reference position. Let a be the mean of the global periodic first-order response, so on I one has r1=z_p+a. The arbitrary constant a is retained: no exact mean or periodicity of the full nonlinear family is asserted. The oscillating part of the first-order dipole coefficient $q(r_1-a)$ is $\operatorname{Re}(p_0e^{-i\omega t})$ with complex amplitude $$p_0=-\frac{q^2}{m\omega^2}\,e\,e^{i\kappa\cdot x_0};$$ equivalently $p_0=\alpha e'$ with $\alpha=-\frac{q^2}{m\omega^2}$ (units $\mathrm F\,\mathrm m^2$) and the unimodular factor $e'=e\,e^{i\kappa\cdot x_0}$, $|e'|=|e|$. (c) [Leading Thomson-model cross section] substituting this $p_0$ into [[pthm-em-dipole-scattering-cross-section]](b) gives $$\sigma_{\rm T}=\frac{q^4}{6\pi\varepsilon_0^2m^2c^4}=\frac{8\pi}{3}\Bigl(\frac{q^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0mc^2}\Bigr)^2,$$ independent of $\omega$ and of the phase factor. (d) [Scope] this is a controlled conditional first variation of the adopted relativistic external-force law under the stated solution-family hypotheses. It is not the exact Newtonian force postulate, it does not assert existence, persistence, stability or self-consistency of the family, it excludes self-force, radiation reaction and material media, and it makes no empirical, measurement, atomic-physics or frequency-response claim. In(a), every local r1 has the unique global harmonic extension z_p+a+bt, with z_p=Re(-w omega^-2 exp(-i omega t)), b=r1'(0)-z_p'(0), a=r1(0)-z_p(0). Thus the general affine-drift response is also retained; preparation(P) sets b0 for(b),(c) and leaves a arbitrary. For a nonzero eta, the associated LEADING ideal harmonic model has incident amplitude eta e and induced dipole amplitude eta p0. Their squared flux factors eta² cancel in its cross-section ratio; sigma_T is this leading-model coefficient, not an assertion of the exact nonlinear particle's emitted field or cross section. At q0 the induced amplitude and sigma_T are zero without any division by q. All eta estimates apply only to the open parameter domain on which the family was declared.
items.strategy:
Use the exact integrated momentum ODE; never differentiate a uniform-in-time Oeta² remainder. Fix a compact K in I and choose a closed interval L contained in I that contains K and0. Put v_eta=r_eta', gamma_eta=(1-|v_eta|²/c²)^-1/2, and P_eta=m gamma_eta v_eta. The stated family expansion implies r_eta->x0 and v_eta/eta->r1' uniformly on L as eta->0 with eta!=0, and |v_eta|=O(|eta|). For small eta the fixed speed bound |v_eta|/c<=1/2 holds on L; the actual algebraic low-speed clause of [[pthm-em-relativistic-lorentz-force]] gives gamma_eta=1+O(eta²) uniformly. Hence P_eta/eta->m r1' uniformly, using only multiplication of uniformly bounded functions.
The EXACT coordinate ODE of that supplier is
$$P_\eta'(t)=q\eta\,[E_{\rm inc}(r_\eta(t),t)+v_\eta(t)\times B_{\rm inc}(r_\eta(t),t)].$$
The plane-wave fields are smooth with bounded spatial first derivatives on a common compact tube around x0 times L, so their values at r_eta converge uniformly to their values at x0; the magnetic term is uniformly Oeta since B is bounded and v_eta=Oeta. Thus for eta!=0, P_eta'/eta converges uniformly to q E_inc(x0,t). This derivative convergence comes from the adopted ODE, not from differentiating the family expansion. Apply componentwise scalar FTC [[thm-ftc-second-part]] to the actual C1 momentum on [0,t], with oriented limits for t<0:
$$\frac{P_\eta(t)-P_\eta(0)}\eta=q\int_0^t[E_{\rm inc}(r_\eta(s),s)+v_\eta(s)\times B_{\rm inc}(r_\eta(s),s)]ds.$$
Uniform convergence passes through these finite ordinary integrals: each component's error is at most the interval length times its uniform supremum, by [[lem-integral-elementary-bounds]]. Taking the limit gives
$$m[r_1'(t)-r_1'(0)]=q\int_0^tE_{\rm inc}(x_0,s)ds.$$
The continuous integrand and [[thm-ftc-first-part]] now imply m r1''=q E_inc(x0,t) on I. This proves(a) and the available first-order equation while retaining the original position/velocity assumptions and arbitrary local I; no differentiability in eta beyond the given uniform expansion and no acceleration-error differentiation is assumed. The parameter endpoints eta=+-eta0 are never evaluated. A continuous differentiable family was not replaced by a stronger C2-in-eta family.
By the LOCAL interval/global extension clause(d) of [[lem-em-harmonic-forcing-periodic-response]] with w=(q/m)e exp(i kappa dot x0), r1=z_p+a+bt on I and its explicit extension on R is unique. Preparation(P) says this extension is periodic, hence b0; this is nonvacuous even when I is shorter than a period. Its mean a comes from the harmonic lemma's finite-period mean calculation. Therefore q(r1-a)=Re[-q² e exp(i kappa dot x0) exp(-i omega t)/(m omega²)], proving(b), with the arbitrary constant mean retained and x0 only the zeroth-order reference position. The phase factor has modulus1 by [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]], so |p0|=q²|e|/(m omega²) and p0=alpha e', alpha=-q²/(m omega²).
Substituting into [[pthm-em-dipole-scattering-cross-section]](b) cancels omega^4 and gives sigma_T=q^4/(6pi epsilon0²m²c^4)=(8pi/3)[q²/(4pi epsilon0 m c²)]². The formula is for the leading ideal harmonic model: for nonzero eta scale BOTH incident amplitude and harmonic dipole amplitude by eta, so their ratio is unchanged. At q0 the same algebra gives zero response amplitude and zero cross section. The adopted external-force law excludes self-field and material/recoil forces; neither the local solution-family assumption nor the global extension of its LINEAR response proves global persistence/periodicity of the nonlinear family or a self-consistent scattered field. Finite-interval FTC, uniform limits and harmonic affine classification are choice-free; only the stated cross-section source/sphere premise carries Countable Choice.

items.title: Uniform rectangular aperture: the Fraunhofer sinc-squared pattern
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by [[pthm-em-scalar-aperture-diffraction]] and by the Riemann-Lebesgue comparison and Fubini suppliers used in the integral reduction below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Work in the scalar aperture model of [[post-em-scalar-aperture-model]] and [[pthm-em-scalar-aperture-diffraction]], with frequency $\omega>0$, $k=\omega/c$, aperture plane $y_3=0$, model field $u=G_k*\alpha$ and $I(x)=\frac12|u(x)|^2$. Fix $a>0$, $b>0$ and $A_0\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$; identify the rectangle $R:=[-a,a]\times[-b,b]\subset\mathbb R^2$ with the planar aperture $\{(y_1,y_2,0):(y_1,y_2)\in R\}$ and take the **uniform rectangular aperture distribution** let $\iota:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R^3$ be $\iota(y_1,y_2)=(y_1,y_2,0)$, and define its plane-embedding pushforward $$\alpha(E):=A_0\,\lambda_2(R\cap\iota^{-1}(E))\qquad(E\subseteq\mathbb R^3\text{ Borel}).$$ This is a finite complex measure on $\mathbb R^3$, supported on the embedded compact rectangle $S=\iota(R)$ with $|y|\le a':=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$ and total variation $\|\alpha\|_{\rm TV}=4ab|A_0|$ ([[def-multidimensional-rectangle-and-volume]], [[def-measure-with-density]], [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]]). Then: (a) [Fraunhofer amplitude] with $\operatorname{sinc}\xi:=\sin\xi/\xi$ for $\xi\ne0$ and $\operatorname{sinc}0:=1$, the Fraunhofer amplitude factor of [[pthm-em-scalar-aperture-diffraction]](a) is exactly $$\int e^{-ikn\cdot y}\,d\alpha(y)=4abA_0\operatorname{sinc}(ka\,n_1)\operatorname{sinc}(kb\,n_2)\qquad(n=(n_1,n_2,n_3)\in S^2),$$ an identity for every direction $n$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-complex-exponential]], [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]], [[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]], [[thm-continuous-on-a-rectangle-is-riemann-integrable]], [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]], [[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]). (b) [Fraunhofer intensity] in the Fraunhofer regime of [[pthm-em-scalar-aperture-diffraction]](a) with aperture radius $a':=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$, i.e. for $r\ge2a'$, the model intensity is $$I_{\rm F}(rn)=\frac{a^2b^2|A_0|^2}{2\pi^2r^2}\operatorname{sinc}^2(ka\,n_1)\operatorname{sinc}^2(kb\,n_2)$$ up to the Fraunhofer absolute error of that theorem, transferred to $I$ by its clause (c). The pattern vanishes exactly where $ka\,n_1\in\pi\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$ or $kb\,n_2\in\pi\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$, and, as a mathematical pattern on all $S^2$, has its global maximum exactly at the two poles $n=(0,0,\pm1)$. The model observes only $x_3>0$; its allowed directions have $n_3>0$, where the central maximum is only $n=(0,0,1)$. (c) [Scope] this is an exact computation inside the adopted ideal scalar model, not a measured diffraction record: no absolute radiometric calibration, polarization content, screen interaction, apparatus model or sampling law is asserted, and the Fraunhofer/Fresnel error bounds of [[pthm-em-scalar-aperture-diffraction]] are inherited rather than re-estimated.
items.strategy: (a) The continuous embedding $\iota$ has Borel inverse images by [[thm-continuous-preimages-of-borel-sets-are-borel]]. Disjoint Borel sets have disjoint inverse images; countable additivity of $\lambda_2$ therefore proves directly that the displayed $\alpha$ is a complex measure as in [[def-complex-measure]]. It is supported on $S=\iota(R)$. For every countable partition, the sum of the moduli of its values is $|A_0|\lambda_2(R)=4ab|A_0|$ by [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]], so [[def-total-variation-of-a-signed-or-complex-measure]] gives the stated finite total variation. For a simple Borel $f$ on $\mathbb R^3$ the defining sum gives $\int f\,d\alpha=A_0\int_Rf(\iota(y))\,d\lambda_2(y)$; uniform finite-simple approximations of any bounded Borel $f$ and the total-variation bound pass this identity to the integrals of [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]]. Thus the plane measure is correctly typed for the three-dimensional model. For $f(y)=e^{-ik(n_1y_1+n_2y_2)}$ (the $y_3$-coordinate is zero on the aperture, and $n\cdot y=n_1y_1+n_2y_2$ by [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), $f$ is continuous on the compact rectangle $R$ ([[thm-continuous-on-a-rectangle-is-riemann-integrable]]), so [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]] identifies the Lebesgue integral with the Riemann double integral; [[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]] factors it into the product of the two one-dimensional integrals. For $n_1\ne0$, the one-dimensional integral is $\int_{-a}^a e^{-ikn_1y_1}\,dy_1=2\sin(ka\,n_1)/(kn_1)=2a\operatorname{sinc}(ka\,n_1)$ by [[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]] and [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] and [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]] for the affine phase $y_1\mapsto-kn_1y_1$, applied to the real and imaginary parts via [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]; for $n_1=0$ it equals $2a=2a\operatorname{sinc}0$ by the separately defined value, so the formula holds for every direction. The second factor is analogous, giving the displayed product $4abA_0\operatorname{sinc}(ka\,n_1)\operatorname{sinc}(kb\,n_2)$. (b) Insert the product amplitude into the Fraunhofer expression $u(rn)=\frac{e^{ikr}}{4\pi r}\int e^{-ikn\cdot y}d\alpha(y)+$error of [[pthm-em-scalar-aperture-diffraction]](a), square the modulus and use $I=\frac12|u|^2$; the modulus of the amplitude is $4ab|A_0||\operatorname{sinc}(ka\,n_1)||\operatorname{sinc}(kb\,n_2)|$, so $|u_{\rm F}|^2=\frac{a^2b^2|A_0|^2}{\pi^2r^2}\operatorname{sinc}^2(ka\,n_1)\operatorname{sinc}^2(kb\,n_2)$ and the factor $\frac12$ gives the displayed $I_{\rm F}$. The zero assertion follows from [[thm-sine-cosine-zero-sets-and-fundamental-period]] and the separate value at0. To prove the exact maxima, $|\sin x|<|x|$ for every $x\ne0$: for $x>0$ set $\delta=\min\{x/3,\pi/6\}>0$. On $[\delta,2\delta]$, the cosine signs and strict monotonicity of [[thm-sine-cosine-signs-monotonicity-and-ranges]] give $|\cos t|\le\cos\delta<1$, while globally $|\cos t|\le1$. FTC and the Riemann integral triangle/monotonicity estimate (applied to $-|\cos|\le\cos\le|\cos|$) give $|\sin x|\le\int_0^x|\cos t|\,dt\le x-\delta(1-\cos\delta)<x$; continuous integrability and subinterval additivity are supplied by [[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]], [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]] and [[thm-additivity-over-subintervals]]. Negative $x$ follows from sine oddness in [[cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity]]. Thus $|\operatorname{sinc}x|=1$ exactly at0, and since $k,a,b>0$ the product attains its maximum exactly when $n_1=n_2=0$, the two spherical poles. Only the positive pole belongs to the model upper half-space. The embedded corners have norm exactly $a'=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$; the support lies in the closed radius set $|y|\le a'$, so the parent theorem's directly proved closed-support estimate applies at the unchanged endpoint $r\ge2a'$; clause (c) of the theorem transfers the field error to $I$. (c) is the scope of the model; no additional approximation is introduced. The computation uses only the standard Riemann/Lebesgue and trigonometric suppliers listed in the dependencies; the Countable Choice assumption is exactly the one carried by the Riemann-Lebesgue comparison and Fubini interfaces, with no additional choice.
